story.conflict: A designer must refuse to validate her brother's invented work history while their parents frame the lie as harmless family help.
story.hook: Her brother applied for a design job with her portfolio. He'd listed her as an employee he'd supervised.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF HELP DOESNT MEAN LYING
story.premise: A man applies for a design job with his sister's portfolio and lists her as an employee he supervised.
story.punchline: This time, he had to make the first mark.
story.script: Maya saw the application on Daniel's laptop. Under her bakery logo, he'd written that he led the project. The bakery belonged to their mother. Maya had drawn that logo at her kitchen table while Daniel was away traveling. He said the interviewer wanted a reference, and she'd only have to confirm a few things. Their mother said getting his foot in the door wouldn't hurt anybody. Maya asked whose work he'd show once he was inside. Daniel said he could learn. Then he asked why the bread in the logo formed a letter instead of looking like bread. Maya told him to answer that as the person who'd supposedly directed her. He couldn't. Their mother said Maya was making him feel small. Maya said he'd named her as his assistant to make himself look bigger. Daniel asked whether she could explain that one design before the interview. She slid him a blank sheet instead. He pushed it away. She said she could help him learn, but wouldn't tell an employer he'd supervised work he hadn't done. Daniel stared at the application. Then he called the recruiter and said the portfolio wasn't his. Maya stayed while he made the call. Afterward, he asked whether the blank paper was still an offer. She handed him a pencil. This time, he had to make the first mark.
story.twist: The brother needs his sister to explain the work because he cannot describe the decisions behind the designs he claims to have directed.

youtube.description: A designer discovers her brother has claimed her portfolio and wants her to confirm that he supervised her work.
youtube.title: The Assistant He Named on His Application

story.conflict: A bride must respond to her mother's financial distress without accepting that needing help gives her permission to borrow secretly.
story.hook: A bride caught her mother taking cash from the wedding gifts. She was leaving IOUs and saying the couple didn't need the money yet.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE SHOULD HAVE ASKED
story.premise: A bride catches her mother taking cash from the wedding gifts and replacing it with IOUs because she thinks the couple can wait for their money.
story.punchline: This time, she waited for her daughter to open it.
story.script: Beth found her behind the gift table with an open envelope and two thousand dollars in her handbag. Her mother, Carol, said she was keeping track. Every envelope had a note saying she'd replace what she'd borrowed. Beth asked when she'd agreed to lend it. Carol said they were going on a honeymoon; she was trying to keep a roof over her head. Beth asked what that meant. Carol hadn't paid last month's rent. She'd lost some cleaning work and been too ashamed to say. Beth closed the door so the guests wouldn't hear. Then Carol said surely Beth could wait for the money. Beth asked why she hadn't called before taking it. Carol looked at the handbag. She said she'd been afraid Beth would say no. Beth told her that meant she'd known there was a choice to ask about. Carol started putting the notes back into the envelopes. Beth asked her to put back the cash instead. She said they'd sit down tomorrow and work out what help was possible. Carol asked whether she was still allowed in the photographs. Beth said she'd closed the door to talk to her, not send her away. Her mother emptied the handbag onto the table. They counted the money back together. Then Carol handed Beth the last unopened envelope. This time, she waited for her daughter to open it.
story.twist: The mother has overdue rent and hid her need out of shame, but taking the gifts has turned asking for help into deciding for the couple.

youtube.description: A bride catches her mother borrowing wedding cash without permission, then learns why she was afraid to ask.
youtube.title: The IOUs Behind the Wedding Gift Table

story.conflict: A dismissed employee must decide whether to sign a false resignation to receive the pay her employer is withholding.
story.hook: Her boss fired her, then asked her to pay five hundred dollars for quitting. Her wages were on the desk, but he wouldn't hand them over.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF FIRING WAS HIS DECISION
story.premise: A boss fires an employee and then demands a five-hundred-dollar resignation fee before releasing her final wages.
story.punchline: there was no resignation with her name on it.
story.script: Ruth had refused an unpaid Sunday shift. Her boss, Colin, told her not to come back, then placed a resignation form beside her pay envelope. She asked why she'd be resigning from a job he'd ended. He pointed to a five-hundred-dollar leaving fee in his staff agreement. Ruth asked where it said she'd chosen to leave. Colin pushed a pen toward her and said signing would make everything simpler. She asked whether the envelope held all her wages. He said it did, but he'd deduct the fee unless she paid separately. Ruth said she wasn't signing that she had quit. Colin called her difficult and asked a coworker to witness that he'd offered to settle. The coworker, Sam, asked what he was witnessing. Ruth said Colin had fired her and was keeping her pay until she signed a resignation. Colin told Sam to get back to work. Sam stayed. Ruth asked Colin to write those terms on the form himself. He said she was making accusations. She asked which part he hadn't just said. Colin looked at the envelope, then tore the resignation across the signature line. He handed over the full wages and told her he never wanted to employ her again. Ruth counted the cash before leaving. Outside, Sam asked whether she had another job. She didn't. She had her pay, and there was no resignation with her name on it.
story.twist: The boss needs her signature to describe his dismissal decision as her voluntary departure and justify the fee he wants to collect.

youtube.description: A boss demands a resignation fee from the employee he just fired, with her final wages sitting on his desk.
youtube.title: Five Hundred Dollars for the Job He Ended

story.conflict: Employees must protect their promised time off without letting their employer use innocent passengers as a reason to demand unpaid labor.
story.hook: Her boss admitted tricking the staff into an unpaid shift. Their free cruise had already left port with paying dinner guests aboard.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF A REWARD ISNT A SHIFT
story.premise: A boss disguises an unpaid catering shift as a staff reward cruise and reveals the paying dinner guests only after the boat leaves port.
story.punchline: The view was finally hers to enjoy.
story.script: Lily had put her feet up when the aprons appeared. Her restaurant boss, Victor, said the buffet needed setting out and the tables needed clearing. This was the reward trip he'd promised after their busiest month. Lily asked when he'd intended to mention the work. He said if he'd called it a shift, nobody would have come. Across the deck, a passenger asked when the dinner she'd paid for would start. Victor handed Lily an apron and told her not to ruin the evening. Lily said he'd sold the dinner. She hadn't. He said the boat trip was worth more than their usual wages. One of the cooks said he'd rather have been paid at home. Victor said he couldn't serve forty people alone. Lily asked what he'd have done if his staff hadn't accepted the reward. He had no answer. She offered to work at her normal rate if he paid her, but said nobody else had to. Two coworkers agreed; the others wanted their evening off. Victor said paying them would eat into his profit. The passenger beside him asked whether his price had included staff being paid. He stopped arguing. Before the buffet opened, he transferred the agreed pay and put on an apron himself. Lily served the meal she'd agreed to serve. When her shift ended, she took her seat back. Victor was still clearing tables. The view was finally hers to enjoy.
story.twist: The boss deliberately concealed the work because he knew the staff would not accept it, and must negotiate real consent instead of treating the cruise as payment.

youtube.description: A staff reward cruise becomes an unpaid shift after sailing, until the workers insist that a promised holiday is not permission to use their labor.
youtube.title: The Aprons on the Staff Reward Cruise
